title: Digi-Dan
summary: I built Digi-Dan as the retrieval-augmented backend behind a portfolio assistant, so it can answer questions from curated profile, education, project, skill, and experience data instead of improvising.

images.alt: Digi-Dan chat panel answering a portfolio question with source citations
images.caption: Digi-Dan as presented in its portfolio chat interface.

sections.title: Grounded portfolio conversations
sections.summary: The backend supplies retrieval-grounded answers to a portfolio chat experience.

image.alt: Digi-Dan chat panel answering a portfolio question with source citations
image.caption: Portfolio chat interface powered by Digi-Dan.

problem: A portfolio visitor may ask an open-ended question that a static page cannot anticipate. I needed the assistant to give useful answers from approved material without leaking credentials or falling back to generic, ungrounded chat.
purpose: I built a deployable API that retrieves the most relevant curated knowledge-base chunks, gives them to a generation provider as bounded context, and returns the answer with its source records.
keyFeatures: Retrieval-augmented chat over structured JSON, JSONL, and text knowledge-base content.
Gemini embeddings for retrieval, with Gemini or DeepSeek selectable for answer generation.
Answer payloads that include the matched source records for transparent review and debugging.
A Bearer-protected ingestion endpoint alongside a CLI uploader for vector data.
Allowed-origin checks, a trusted server-to-server bypass, and per-client chat rate limiting.
A Vercel-compatible FastAPI deployment path with GitHub Actions automation for RAG-data uploads.
role: I designed and built the RAG backend and integrated it with the portfolio assistant. My work covered the retrieval and generation flow, ingestion tooling, security boundaries, and the local-to-Vercel deployment path.
technicalHighlights: I use Gemini embeddings to turn each question into a vector query, retrieve the most relevant Upstash Vector chunks, and assemble a character-bounded context before generation.
I keep provider concerns separate: Gemini or DeepSeek can generate the answer, while the retrieval pipeline retains one embedding and vector-index contract.
I return the answer, the selected provider, and the retrieved source records in one response so the portfolio interface can show or inspect its grounding.
I support both operational ingestion paths: a validated, admin-protected API route and a CLI uploader that accepts JSON, JSONL, or plain-text documents.
I separate public browser access from trusted callers with allowed-origin middleware, an X-API-Secret server bypass, a separate Bearer token for ingestion, and per-client chat rate limiting.
I kept the service straightforward to run locally with Uvicorn and deploy on Vercel through a compatible ASGI entrypoint and an Actions-based data-upload workflow.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: A portfolio assistant still needs to handle broad, natural-language questions, but it cannot treat a general model response as a reliable account of someone's work.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: I retrieve focused approved chunks before generation, cap the context passed to the model, and return the matched source records with the answer so the calling interface can review the grounding.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: The public chat experience needs access to the API, while ingestion and trusted server calls must not expose administrative or bypass secrets in browser code.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: I enforce configured browser origins, reserve X-API-Secret for trusted server-to-server calls, protect ingestion with a separate Bearer token, and limit chat requests by client.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Portfolio content changes over time, and manually keeping a vector index in sync would make the assistant stale or fragile.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: I provided a reusable CLI uploader and a GitHub Actions workflow that uploads the RAG data whenever the relevant data or ingestion code changes on main.

resultsImpact: Digi-Dan gives the portfolio a practical way to answer questions beyond the fixed page copy while keeping the conversation anchored to curated material.
Every chat response carries the retrieved source records, which gives the consuming interface a clear basis for review, troubleshooting, and future presentation choices.

The project establishes a reusable, deployment-ready pattern for a portfolio assistant, resume chatbot, documentation assistant, or small knowledge-base chatbot without claiming unverified performance or adoption metrics.
lessonsLearned: I learned that retrieval quality starts with the knowledge base: clear chunk wording, focused topics, and dedicated summaries make broad questions easier to answer well.
Supporting multiple answer providers is useful, but it does not replace a stable embedding model, index dimension, and retrieval contract.
I learned to treat source visibility as part of the product experience, not just a debugging aid; returning sources makes grounded behavior easier to inspect.
I also kept secrets and privileged ingestion firmly on trusted server or automation paths rather than moving convenience into browser code.
